reason: I've had left-sided chest pain for 30 minutes.
diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome, most concerning for myocardial ischemia/infarction, suggested by sudden exertional left-sided pressure-like chest pain with shortness of breath in a smoker with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and recent methamphetamine use.
keyPoints: Character of chest pain: pressure vs pleuritic, radiation, severity, exertional trigger, progression
Associated symptoms: shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, palpitations, dizziness/syncope
Cardiovascular risk factors: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking, stimulant use, family history
Recent cocaine/methamphetamine use and timing relative to pain onset
Alternative causes/red flags: chest trauma from rugby, fever/infection, leg swelling, travel/PE symptoms
Positional features and pleuritic component to consider pericarditis or musculoskeletal pain
transcript:

P: It's just right over on the on the left side.
D: OK, and when did this pain start?
P: It started just 30 minutes ago.

P: Uh, seven.
D: Seven, OK. Have you had ny similar episodes before?

P: Uh I did and it was 38 degrees.

P: Uh, no swelling in my legs.

P: No, my energy has been good. D; Have you been having any kind of thumping or palpitations or feel like your heart has been racing at all?
P: It uhh it does feel like it's beating faster right now. It usually only feels like this when I'm playing sports.

P: No rashes.
D: OK, have you had any cough or runny nose or sore throat? Any kind of those symptoms and in the past month?

D: OK. Just a few more questions. Have you had any diagnosis made by any physician or any anything like diabetes or high blood pressure?

D: OK, and do you take any medications for the these things?

P: No.

P: Um, six days ago.

P: Um, I would say a couple of times a month.
D: A couple of times a month, OK. Alright, and for how long have you been using crystal meth?
P: Uh for the last seven years.
